Page91 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 4.10 CONSTRUCTION PLAN This section outlines the construction, installation and commissioning strategies that have been used to build up the overall cost estimate of the hub. The hub site is be set within an industrial area already having major road and rail links close by and is adjacent to an inlet waterway area of Port Tampa Bay. Thus the site is already well positioned to make use of existing industrial transportation infrastructure in order to minimize construction costs and time. This overview is designed to give an understanding of and a general insight into how the project can be implemented, with its execution based on the following key guiding principles. Safety All works are to be carried out safely, in compliance with all regulations and procedures. Worksite activities should be thoroughly planned for and executed using proven guidelines, with known techniques. Schedule In developing a construction schedule the aim will be to deliver the build works within the agreed timescale while meeting the required safety, quality and cost targets. Starting with the end in mind approach, this is key to construction development, sequencing and optimization. Quality A defined quality strategy should be in place at the outset, ensuring required standards are achieved throughout the construction project. Works carried out off-site at remote fabrication or manufacturing facilities are considered to already have controlled environments, however inspections and quality checks should still be made available and enable monitoring by the project team. This can be reinforced by prioritizing equipment suppliers who have established ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 policies in place. 4.10.1 CONSTRUCTION APPROACH OPTIONS Two main construction / assembly options were identified.  Marine Transportation of Large Pre-Assembled Units  Road / Rail Transportation of smaller components for site integration and erection.
